proposal.title: Pirin v0.8.6
proposal.summary:
## Summary 
 This on-chain upgrade governance proposal is to adopt the Nolus v0.8.6 update for the Nolus Pirin (pirin-1) mainnet which is currently running on v0.8.5. This upgrade introduces the following changes: 

 * **Solana Carrier Module:** A new x/solanacarrier module pins the fee payer placed in Solana transaction carriers and allowlists the carrier instructions. 
 * **CosmWasm Security Patch:** wasmd is updated to v0.61.15 and wasmvm to v3.0.8, applying the latest upstream security fixes. 
 * **Lower Consensus Timeouts:** The recommended timeout_commit value written to node configuration on startup is reduced from 2s to 1.5s, while timeout_propose stays at 2s. This is expected to lower the average block time from the current 2.5s to about 2s. 

 ## On-Chain Upgrade Process 

 At the designated halt height, the Nolus network's state machine will stop functioning temporarily. Validators and node operators must manually replace the existing state machine binary with the updated version. Coordination among validators is encouraged and can be facilitated through the "chat" channel in the "Validators" section on Discord. 
 The target block for this upgrade is **27247000**, estimated to occur on **Wednesday, 7th of October 2026**, at approximately **09:00 UTC**. This estimation assumes an average block time of 2.58 seconds. 

 This upgrade adds the store of the new solanacarrier module and sets its default parameters. 

 Alternatively, validators may leverage Cosmovisor to automate the binary upgrade to v0.8.6. Ensure the latest version is used to successfully implement the upgrade.

proposal.title: Smart Contract Migration (Solana Metis SOL, CB_BTC, WETH - NLS pricing)
proposal.summary:
## Summary 

 The Treasury distributes lender rewards to every registered protocol once per cadence and converts each protocol's reward into NLS through that protocol's own Oracle. The Oracles of `SOLANA-METIS-SOL`, `SOLANA-METIS-CB_BTC` and `SOLANA-METIS-WETH` were instantiated with a minimal LPN → USDC swap tree and their compiled swap-pair tables have no USDC/NLS pair, so the Treasury's dispatch has reverted at every cadence since 2026-09-04 and the time-alarm keeps being re-delivered, burning fees on each attempt. 

 This proposal migrates the three protocols to codes rebuilt from the same release v0.9.1 with the USDC/NLS pair added (nolus-protocol/nolus-networks PR #167): `SOLANA-METIS-SOL` → Lease 956, Leaser 957, LPP 958, Oracle 959, Profit 960, Remote Lease controller 961, Reserve 962; `SOLANA-METIS-CB_BTC` → 963–969; `SOLANA-METIS-WETH` → 970–976 (same order). Each Leaser then migrates its open leases to the new Lease code. `SOLANA-METIS-USDC` is not affected. 

 Three further messages extend each Oracle's swap tree with NLS as a child of USDC (LPN → USDC → NLS), the same way the `SOLANA-METIS-USDC` Oracle already prices NLS via its Solray mirror mint, so the Treasury can convert rewards for every protocol from the first block after migration. 

 By voting "YES" to this proposal you agree to migrate the three protocols and extend their Oracle swap trees.

proposal.title: Unpin Superseded Contract Codes (4/4)
proposal.summary:
## Summary 

 Pinned contract codes stay resident in every node's memory. Over successive protocol releases the Nolus Pirin mainnet has accumulated 345 pinned code IDs, of which only 17 back live contracts today: the platform contracts Treasury (911), Timealarms (912) and Admin (913), and the current `SOLANA-METIS-USDC` (921–927) and `SOLANA-METIS-SOL` (928–934) protocol contracts. The codes stored for the pending v0.9.1 currency update (935–941) are pinned by their own proposal. 

 This is part 4 of 4 of the cleanup; each part unpins a batch of superseded code IDs, because unpinning loads every module at proposal simulation and a single proposal covering all 328 codes exceeds the block gas limit. This part unpins 82 code IDs (830–847, 849–905, 914–920). Each is a superseded release of a platform or protocol contract; no active contract is instantiated from any of them — the only instances left on these codes are closed leases, which never execute again. Unpinning frees node memory and has no effect on contract state or on any contract's ability to execute; an unpinned code is still loaded from storage on demand. 

 By voting "YES" to this proposal you agree to unpin these superseded contract code IDs.

proposal.title: Close Inactive Market (Osmosis Noble USDC)
proposal.summary:
## Summary  

  This proposal concerns the closure of the Osmosis Noble USDC market on the Nolus Pirin (mainnet), which has remained inactive and is no longer serving user demand within the Nolus money market. The closure process is structured to ensure the safe return of user funds and to streamline the protocol by retiring underutilized components.  

  The action will proceed in two steps:  

  **1. Automatic Return of Deposits:** Any remaining deposits in the lending pool will be automatically distributed back to the corresponding lenders. This guarantees that all users are made whole and that no funds remain in the pool.  

  **2. Market Closure:** Following the distribution of funds, the Osmosis Noble USDC market will be fully closed. Users will no longer be able to deposit into the lending pool or open new positions against Osmosis Noble USDC.  

  This measure eliminates maintenance overhead for an inactive market and prepares the protocol for focusing resources on active and strategically valuable markets.  

  By voting "YES" on this proposal, you consent to the automatic distribution of remaining Osmosis Noble USDC deposits to lenders and the full closure of this market as a follow-up action.

 This proposal migrates the protocol contracts of the Solana Metis USDC protocol (`SOLANA-METIS-USDC`) on the Nolus Pirin mainnet to v0.9.1 — Leaser, Lease, LPP, Oracle, Profit, Reserve, and the Remote Lease controller — using the codes pinned by the preceding proposal. With the NLS/USDC pool live on Solana, the price feeders can now publish an NLS price for this protocol.

## Summary

proposal.summary:
## Summary

This proposal adds the newly deployed Solana Metis USDC protocol's Remote Lease controller contract (`nolus1xd9sgdu3lvwm0pzrxg3c3lxwvuwkc6jgzk43zkgzjnndrdp5shvsfv3uzp`) to the Solana relayer allowlist (`solana_allowed_relayers`) in the IBC `02-client` parameters on the Nolus Pirin mainnet (`pirin-1`).

Opening the controller's IBC channel to its Solana counterpart requires it to submit a `MsgChannelOpenInit` against the Solana light client. The chain's `02-client` module treats the signer of that message as a relayer, and the allowlist is fail-closed: until the controller's own address is present, that message is rejected and the channel can never open.

## Proposed Changes

`MsgUpdateParams` replaces the entire `02-client` parameter set, so `allowed_clients` is restated here **unchanged** at its current on-chain value:

* `06-solomachine`
* `07-tendermint`
* `09-localhost`

`solana_allowed_relayers` changes from the three existing relayer operator addresses to those same three plus the Remote Lease controller contract address:

* `nolus1cfzkvsvttuazxrm57v8xyl6v56s3ue5q8u8c5a`
* `nolus1xmaacd2phwny53wwpexkf865hvjnzugrrlgwmd`
* `nolus1t83k9x2cysj7g5lns7j382lhgtzaplpm3c654r`
* `nolus1xd9sgdu3lvwm0pzrxg3c3lxwvuwkc6jgzk43zkgzjnndrdp5shvsfv3uzp` (Solana Metis USDC Remote Lease controller)

## Impact

The three existing relayer operators keep their access unchanged. The added address only grants the Remote Lease controller contract permission to submit Solana light-client channel-handshake messages for its own channel; it grants no other capability. No client type is added or removed, so the IBC connections and channels already in use on `pirin-1` are unaffected.

By voting "YES" on this proposal, you agree to authorize the Solana Metis USDC Remote Lease controller to open its IBC channel on the Nolus Pirin mainnet.

## Summary 

 Oracle market data price feeders are an essential part of the Nolus core architecture which uses its own Oracle system. Each price feeding service is an independent lightweight off-chain component that retrieves prices from configured price providers for a set of denomination pairs. The price feeders utilize a variant of the Exponential Moving Average (EMA) algorithm for the price calculation of any given cryptocurrency pair. Through the use of this algorithm, one can put additional weights on more recently observed prices for a given period. To read more about the role of the price feeders in Nolus, have a look at the [documentation](https://hub.nolus.io/en_US/technical-documentation/oracles-alarms). 

 By voting "YES" on this proposal, you agree to whitelist the five price feeders (pirin-feeder-01 through pirin-feeder-05) for the newly deployed Solana Metis USDC Oracle smart contract. Each service is located in a different geolocation and is configured to push a price every 60 seconds. 

 ## Source code 

 Each price feeding service is built from the [oracle-price-feeder](https://github.com/nolus-protocol/oracle-price-feeder) repository. You can find the configuration for a feeder running on mainnet [here](https://github.com/nolus-protocol/oracle-price-feeder/blob/main/configurations/market-data-feeder.main.toml).

proposal.title: Smart Contract Migration (v0.9.0)
proposal.summary:
## Summary 

 As the Nolus network adopts a semi-permissioned blockchain model, contract migrations require governance approval. The Nolus money market architecture is strategically divided into two main components: the platform core and the protocol core. The platform core houses essential contracts that function universally across various chains without specific modifications for each chain. Conversely, the protocol core is designed for flexibility, allowing for the creation of unique contract instances tailored to each integrated chain, such as Osmosis, Neutron, and others anticipated in the future. This strategic separation ensures that Nolus can scale efficiently while minimizing maintenance overheads. 

 This proposal introduces the migration to a new iteration of smart contracts on the Nolus Pirin mainnet, migrating the platform contracts only — Admin, Timealarms, and Treasury. This release completes the integration of the Solana-side Remote Lease App into the lease lifecycle, including: 
 * **Cross-Chain Wire Format:** Cross-chain lease communication now uses the wire crate's Borsh codec, with coins identified by full ICS-20 denom paths. 
 * **Slippage Protection:** Every swap flow (open, repay, customer close, liquidation) is now floored by a per-scenario max slippage configured on the Leaser. 
 * **Remote Teardown:** Terminal lease states (closed, liquidated) now tear down their remote counterpart through a new CloseRemote step. 

 Existing protocol contracts are not migrated by this release; a protocol moves to v0.9.0 by being closed and re-registered as a fresh deployment. 

 For the complete changelog, please refer to the [release v0.9.0](https://github.com/nolus-protocol/nolus-money-market/releases/tag/v0.9.0) on GitHub. 

 By voting "YES" on this proposal, you consent to the migration of the platform smart contracts to the latest version v0.9.0.
